published.summary: First published Windows build. One-click installer or portable executable — both keep your crosshair library in your roaming profile, so updating never touches your data.
added: Target Monitor selection: put the overlay on any connected display. The choice survives restarts, and the overlay repositions on hotplug, resolution and scaling changes.
Background operation: closing the window hides crshhx to the system tray while overlays, global hotkeys and weapon-slot switching keep running. Quitting is explicit, from the tray menu.

Pro Crosshairs library: 40 curated designs across 8 categories, built into the existing preset system, with an interactive preview bench — backdrops, zoom, colour and size overrides, two-design compare.
Crosshair Academy: 10 tutorials with live in-app demos, labelled illustrations and tracked completion.
One-click Windows installer and a portable executable.
improved: One clean window header: the duplicate native title bar and the File/Edit/View menu bar are gone; clipboard, undo, zoom and DevTools shortcuts still work.
The installer now installs with no prompts. Your data lives outside the install folder, and uninstalling never deletes it.
fixed: The header's minimise, maximise and close buttons were decorative; they now control the window, and close still respects the close-to-tray setting.

published.summary: Gold Series: two fan recreations — Arc Crown and Compact Mark — plus segmented-circle controls in the Designer. Existing libraries, settings and exports load unchanged. Built and checksum-verified by CI on Windows; runtime behaviour on a physical Windows machine has not been tested yet.
added: Gold Series in Pro Crosshairs: Arc Crown (four segmented vermilion arcs around a green centre point) and Compact Mark (a compact green cross with a hollow centre), each with its own category and its attribution shown in the app.
Segmented-circle Designer controls: segment count, arc span and pattern rotation, for any ring-based design.
Crosshair schema v3. The new fields are optional and default to a complete circle, so configurations and export files from earlier versions load unchanged.
improved: The renderer draws genuine SVG arcs for segmented circles instead of approximating them, so the preview and the overlay agree.
Export files stamp the version that wrote them, so an import can report where a library came from.

development.summary: Development notes for the 1.0.0 milestone. Everything below is in the repository and was covered by 1,061 automated tests at the time; it all shipped as part of the 1.1.0 release above.
added: Weapon-slot crosshairs: record a key per slot and switch reticles mid-game without touching the game process.
Crosshair editor with per-arm length and thickness, whole-reticle rotation and scale, inner outline, colour tools with contrast verdicts, undo history and an A/B compare panel.
Preset manager with folders, favourites, descriptions, search and sort; built-in presets can be organised without being modified.
Versioned import and export with a two-step preview: nothing is overwritten unless that entry is set to replace it.
Game profiles with optional foreground-process auto-selection.
ADS morphing (shrink, dot-only, fade) and dynamic firing bloom with a configurable decay.
A live overlay window with F10 to toggle and F9 to cycle presets.
improved: Renderer bundle reduced by 35% by dropping legacy .woff font fallbacks Chromium never reads.
Storage migration runs once per install instead of on every launch.
Packaging configuration for an NSIS installer and a portable executable, with a release workflow that prints measured sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
fixed: Favourites were stored in two places that disagreed with each other.
An import could silently lose a crosshair when two entries wanted the same id.
The storage migration never wrote its completion marker on a fresh install, repeating its probe on every launch.
